title: Why a Tiny Kernel Pops Into Fluffy Popcorn in Seconds
prompt: Create a 45‑60 second vertical explainer on the surprising physics behind popcorn popping. Open with the hook: "Ever wonder why a tiny, hard kernel can burst into a fluffy cloud in seconds?" Then show stock footage of raw kernels, steam, a close‑up of a kernel exploding, and the resulting fluffy popcorn. Explain that each kernel holds just 14% water; when heated, that water turns to super‑heated steam, building pressure until the hull ruptures, instantly turning starch into the airy foam we eat. End with a quick visual of popcorn spilling out of a bowl while the narrator asks, "Now you know the pop‑secret behind your snack!"

title: Why Leaves Turn Red in Autumn – The Science Behind Fall Colors

Open with the hook: “Ever wonder why trees suddenly dress in reds and golds every fall?” Build the story with stock footage of forest canopies, close‑ups of green leaves turning yellow, orange, red, and time‑lapse of sunrise/sunset over the forest. End with a quick visual of a leaf’s cross‑section showing pigments.
